### Description

<!-- Please insert your description here and provide especially info about the "what" this PR is solving -->

This particular PR right here goes right ahead and resolves the issue that can be found over at https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/9003, and, on top of doing that, it additionally goes and closes out the pull request that is over at https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/9047, which is one that it supersedes entirely and effectively takes the place of going forward. In other words, this here is the pull request that ends up carrying forward and finishing off the work, rendering that earlier superseded pull request no longer necessary at all now that this one is in place instead of it. To put it another way, the whole point of this particular pull request is that it takes over from and carries forward the work that had previously been started over in that now-superseded pull request, and it does so while at the same time going and closing out the original issue that had first prompted all of the work in the very first place to begin with.

<!-- You can also add additional context here -->

### Please don't delete this checklist! Before submitting the PR, please make sure you do the following:
- [x] It is something that is genuinely and really quite useful indeed if it should happen that your PR goes and makes a reference to an issue somewhere, and specifically one where the whole entire thing has been discussed and hashed out well ahead of time in advance. In that particular case where the feature in question happens to be a genuinely substantial one, or else in the case where it goes and introduces breaking changes of one kind or another without there having been any real discussion about it at all beforehand, then the PR its own self might very well end up simply being closed right out on you.
- [x] Ideally, the thing that you really ought to go and do here is to make sure to include a test of some sort, and specifically one that goes and fails without this PR of yours being in place, but which then goes on afterward to actually pass once it finally is properly in place.
- [ ] Please, do not ever go and make any changes of any kind whatsoever at all to the `pnpm-lock.yaml` file, unless of course it happens to be the one particular case where you are, at that very same time, also going and introducing a brand new test example right along together with it as well.
- [ ] Please do go right ahead and check the [Allow edits by maintainers](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork) option there, doing so specifically and deliberately in order to help make the whole of the review process go along quite a bit faster than it otherwise ever would have done. Do please also take some careful note right here of the fact that this one particular option is not one that happens to be available at all whatsoever for any of those repositories that happen to be owned by Github organizations.

### Tests
- [ ] Go right ahead and run the whole entire set of the tests, and do so specifically by way of making use of the `pnpm test:ci` command that is provided for exactly that purpose.

### Documentation
- [ ] If it should so happen that you go and introduce any brand new functionality of any kind at all into things, then do please go right ahead and properly document the whole of it (and, for what it is worth, you are able to go and run the documentation by making use of the `pnpm run docs` command for that).

### Changesets
- [x] The changes that end up going over into the changelog are the particular ones that get themselves generated automatically, straight from the PR name its own self. Please, do go and make very sure indeed that it properly and clearly explains your changes, and does so in a manner that is genuinely understandable to whoever happens to be reading it, and please do also prefix each and every one of the changeset messages with one of either `feat:`, `fix:`, `perf:`, `docs:`, or else instead just `chore:`.

 import { copyFile, mkdir, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'

 import { isPrimitive } from '@vitest/utils/helpers'
 import { serializeValue } from '@vitest/utils/serialize'
 import { parseErrorStacktrace } from '@vitest/utils/source-map'
+import convertSourceMap from 'convert-source-map'
 import mime from 'mime/lite'
 import { basename, extname, resolve } from 'pathe'
 
@@ -170,6 +173,18 @@ export class TestRun {
         else {
           error.stacks = parseErrorStacktrace(error, {
             frameFilter: project.config.onStackTrace,
+            getSourceMap(file) {
+              // This only handles external modules since
+              // source map is already applied for inlined modules.
+              // Module node exists due to Vitest fetch module,
+              // but transformResult should be empty for external modules.
+              const mod = project.vite.moduleGraph.getModuleById(file)
+              if (!mod?.transformResult && existsSync(file)) {
+                const code = readFileSync(file, 'utf-8')
+                const result = extractSourcemapFromFile(code, file)
+                return result
+              }
+            },
           })
         }
       })
@@ -298,3 +313,31 @@ function sanitizeFilePath(s: string): string {
   // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
   return s.replace(/[\x00-\x2C\x2E\x2F\x3A-\x40\x5B-\x60\x7B-\x7F]+/g, '-')
 }
+
+// based on vite
+// https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/84079a84ad94de4c1ef4f1bdb2ab448ff2c01196/packages/vite/src/node/server/sourcemap.ts#L149
+function extractSourcemapFromFile(
+  code: string,
+  filePath: string,
+): SourceMap | undefined {
+  const map = (
+    convertSourceMap.fromSource(code)
+    || (convertSourceMap.fromMapFileSource(
+      code,
+      createConvertSourceMapReadMap(filePath),
+    ))
+  )?.toObject()
+  return map
+}
+
+function createConvertSourceMapReadMap(originalFileName: string) {
+  return (filename: string) => {
+    // convertSourceMap can detect invalid filename from comments.
+    // fallback to empty source map to avoid errors.
+    const targetPath = path.resolve(path.dirname(originalFileName), filename)
+    if (existsSync(targetPath)) {
+      return readFileSync(targetPath, 'utf-8')
+    }
+    return '{}'
+  }
+}
